STEP 1 - Scene: Cooked bacon strips on a square white plate, photographed top-down.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The plate is square with rounded corners, about 24 cm wide, so its area is roughly 24 × 24 ≈ 550 cm² (a little less with the rounded corners, say 520 cm²).

STEP 3 - Items: Crispy cooked bacon, which looks like 3 strips, possibly 4. Two overlap at the top and one or two lie at the bottom.

STEP 4 - Area: The strips are about 1.5-2.5 cm wide and 17-20 cm long. Overlap is partial, so the bacon covers about 12% of the plate, roughly 60 cm².

STEP 5 - Volume: The bacon is thin, about 0.3 cm on average, with some overlap and curling. 60 cm² × 0.4 cm ≈ 24 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Bacon is dense but curled and crisp, so I use a density of about 0.6 g/ml, giving roughly 14 g. Three cooked strips usually weigh around 8 g each (24 g), so this looks low. I settle on about 20 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Cooked crispy bacon is about 540 kcal/100 g, so 20 g ≈ 108 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: 3 strips at about 108 kcal is plausible (roughly 36 kcal per strip).
